summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for chest pain that occurred during walking at his dialysis center. The pain was associated with nausea and vomiting, and did not respond to sublingual nitroglycerin. He was treated with morphine in the emergency department and admitted for evaluation of unstable angina. Initial ECG showed T-wave flattening and ST depression, but troponin levels remained stable. A cardiac catheterization revealed in-stent restenosis in the left circumflex artery and a narrowing at the origin of the LAD, both of which were treated with percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty without stent placement. He remained pain-free post-procedure, received two hemodialysis sessions during admission, and was discharged home in stable condition. Medications were adjusted, including uptitration of metoprolol and lisinopril, and he was given clear instructions on activity, diet, weight monitoring, and follow-up care.
